revision: rev5 — 2026-07-27. Adds X-DRY-MIX after the second holdout (seed 2026072702, 92/100) found `Puddings, tapioca, dry mix` resolving to the eligible role `sweet`. rev4 notes follow. Adds `recipePostPass` after measuring the rev3 rules against all 1,500 authored recipes: 198 of them (13.2%) resolved to spice or herb, including a 13-ingredient khichdi, and 79 more fell to `other`. Commodity name rules cannot classify dish titles. rev3 notes follow. Corrects the six defects the MP-7 60-row holdout exposed at 47/60: bare `salt` at priority 80 was misclassifying 592 catalogue rows as spice, and `juice`, `sauce`, `cream`, `milk`, `water`, `butter` and `oil` carried the same shape (~2,000 rows of exposure); all 187 categories ran above the name phrases even though 57.7% of rows sit under a coarse top-level bucket; and `nonFood` conflated non-nutritive rows with ingredient-only rows. Fixes: a firstSegment match scope, a three-way sensitive/fine/coarse category split, and a new `ingredientOnly` role. THE 60-ROW HOLDOUT IS NOW BURNED — these rules were written after seeing its failures, so it is training data from here on and a fresh holdout is mandatory. rev2 notes follow. Corrects all three signal-driven rules after the MP-7 signal audit: `recipe.course` did not exist; `usda.foodCategory` was the wrong field name with the wrong 25-value vocabulary; `dravya.classification` supplied Sanskrit keys with zero overlap with the data. All three are now bound to real fields with their real vocabularies, read directly from the repo. rev1 context follows.  Written after MP-6b produced culinarily absurd plans that passed all 23 hard properties: infant formula served to adults three times in one week, a breakfast of four chocolate drinks, and a dinner of six dried herbs beside raw lentils. Nothing in the catalogue said what a row IS FOR. This file says it.
author: Director
appliesTo: Every row of the 14,484-item FoodItem catalogue, plus the 1,500 authored recipes. Consumed by the MP-5 solver as an eligibility and composition constraint, and by properties C1-C9 of plan-validity-properties.json as their vocabulary.
whyThisExists: minAgeMonths is a FLOOR, not a range. Infant formula carries a floor of 0 and therefore satisfies every adult age check in the system. The catalogue can express 'not before this age' and cannot express 'intended for infants, inappropriate for adults'. It also cannot express 'this is a seasoning, not a dish'. Both failures produced the same symptom in MP-6b. A role is the missing field.

matching.reuse: Reuse the food-concepts.json rev5 matcher — same normalization, same contiguous token-sequence phrase match, same order-independent vetoTokens, same suffix negation, token-boundary only and NEVER substring. Do not write a second matcher.

pluralTolerance.spec: A phrase token matches a catalogue token when they are identical, or differ by a trailing 's', or by a trailing 'es', or by y->ies, or appear together in irregularPlurals below. Case-folded.
pluralTolerance.FC1_DEFECT: food-concepts.json rev5 specifies trailing-'s' ONLY. That rule does not match 'potatoes' from 'potato', 'tomatoes' from 'tomato', 'berries' from 'berry', or 'leaves' from 'leaf'. It was caught here by running this file's own goldens against its own rules: 'Potatoes, flesh and skin, raw' — the exact row that produced the FC-1 `flesh` defect — resolved to `other`. The same fix must be applied to food-concepts.json and its 117 exclusion goldens re-run. Tracked as FC-1f in TASK-MP7.md.

resolution.algorithm: Evaluate EVERY rule against the row. Collect all that match. Take the highest `priority`. Break ties by longest matched phrase in tokens; break remaining ties by the order rules appear in this file. A rule with `vetoTokens` or `vetoPhrases` that fires is discarded before priority is considered.

priorityBands.85: authored recipe course — real data, outranks every name guess
priorityBands.80: name phrases strong enough to override the USDA category

resolution.singleAssignment: Exactly one role per row. Unlike food-concepts.json, roles are not a set and do not roll up a hierarchy.

roles.definition: The protein or legume centre of a meal, or a composed dish that stands alone.
Grain, bread, tuber or other starch base.
Vegetable, fruit, dairy accompaniment, nuts, salad.
Dried seed, bark, root or powder used for seasoning. Includes salt.
Classical therapeutic dravya taken in small measured quantity.
Chutney, pickle, sauce, dressing, dip served alongside.
Cooking or finishing fat: oil, ghee, butter.
Protein powder, medical food, vitamin, meal replacement.
Infant or toddler formula, baby food, pediatric nutrition.
roles.exception: Eligible ONLY when the profile age is under 36 months, in which case it may be an anchor.

roles.definition: Real food that is not a served dish: pie crust, flour, dough, batter, dry mix. Requires further preparation to become a component.
Not nutritive: leavening, thickener, colouring, plain water.
Unresolved. Eligible but never an anchor, and capped, so an unresolved row can never constitute a meal.

rules.note: Order-independent because USDA writes both 'Infant formula, ...' and 'Formula, infant, ...'.

A bare 'formula' row in a food catalogue is an infant product until shown otherwise. Misrouting between infantProduct and supplement is HARMLESS here: both are ineligible as meal components, so this rule is allowed to be blunt.

rev3, added after the MP-7 holdout. rev2's `nonFood` conflated two different things: rows that are not nutritive at all (baking soda, tap water, colouring) and rows that ARE food but are not a served dish (pie crust, flour, dry mix, batter). The holdout labeller correctly called an unbaked pie crust ingredient-only; the resolver called it `staple`; and the disagreement counted as a sensitive-role error because my definition had merged the two. Both remain ineligible as components, so nothing about plan safety changes — but the taxonomy can now express what the labeller meant.

rev5, added after the second MP-7 holdout flagged 'Puddings, tapioca, dry mix' as an eligibility-crossing error. A dry mix is ingredient-only ONLY when the name does not also say it has been made up. FNDDS carries both forms of nearly every row: 'Puddings, tapioca, dry mix' is a powder, 'Pudding, tapioca, made from dry mix' is a dessert, and 'Hot chocolate / cocoa, dry mix, made with water' is a drink. A blunt dry+mix rule captures 101 rows and is wrong on 13 of them; with the preparedIndicators it captures 88 and I could not find a wrong one. `not reconstituted` overrides the `reconstituted` indicator — the negation is checked as a contiguous phrase before the indicator is.
rules.evaluation: 1. require a tokenGroup hit. 2. if `negatedIndicator` matches as a contiguous phrase, the rule FIRES regardless of indicators. 3. otherwise if any preparedIndicator matches contiguously, the rule does not fire. 4. otherwise it fires.

rules.note: Ingredient-only or non-nutritive rows. Ineligible as components. NOT the same as fat or condiment.

rev2 CORRECTION. rev1 named a field `recipe.course` that DOES NOT EXIST. The real fields are `meal` (breakfast 155 / lunch 569 / dinner 367 / snack 163 / drink 133 / dessert 113) and `category` (classical 300 / everyday 563 / international 637). Only two `meal` values carry role information directly: a recipe whose meal is `drink` IS a beverage, and one whose meal is `dessert` IS a sweet. The other four name a SLOT, not a role, and mapping them here would be exactly the proxy substitution this file forbids. They are handled structurally at priority 45 instead.

Deliberately placed BELOW the 60-band name phrases, so it is a fallback and never an override. The claim it makes is structural, not inferential: a row with two or more ingredients and at least one preparation step is a prepared dish, therefore it is not a raw commodity and not a seasoning. Name rules still win where they fire — 'Bathua Raita' resolves to side, 'Dry Fruit Ladoo' to sweet, 'Cilantro Coriander Herb Salt' to spice — and only recipes whose names give no signal fall through here. Accuracy is gated separately in TASK-MP7 §4 G2b because this is the weakest rule in the file.
Lemon/lime juice is a condiment-scale ingredient, not a drink; vetoed here and caught by C-LEMONJUICE.
Vetoes exist because 'coconut milk' and 'milk powder' are cooking ingredients, not drinks.
Overrides the 'Soups, Sauces, and Gravies' category, which otherwise routes to condiment.

The vetoes stop 'Fish, tuna, canned in oil, drained' from resolving to fat. This is the single most likely place for this file to go wrong, because 'oil' appears as a preparation word across hundreds of rows.

At 80 rather than 60 because the fine category 'Nuts and seeds' maps to `side` at 70 and would otherwise win, giving a 40-250 g portion range to a spread eaten 15 g at a time. NOTE: this contradicts the rev1 golden case 'Peanut butter, smooth style -> side', which I wrote and which was wrong. The golden is corrected to `condiment` in food-role-goldens rev2; see the disclosure in TASK-MP7 §3.

Any category that maps to an ineligible role sits ABOVE the name phrases and stays there. Demoting 'Baby food: fruit' below a name rule would let the token 'apple' turn an infant product into a side dish. The one rule in this file that must never lose a tie.
The granular WWEIA-style values. Specific enough to outrank a name phrase.

rev3, added after the MP-7 holdout. rev2 ran ALL 187 categories at priority 70, above the name phrases. But 7,268 of 12,601 rows (57.7%) sit under one of these coarse SR Legacy top-level buckets, so for the MAJORITY of the catalogue the role was being decided by the least specific signal available, overriding a name phrase that knew more. That is why 'Cookies, chocolate chip' resolved to `staple` via 'Baked Products' and 'Fish, halibut, raw' resolved to `other` via 'American Indian/Alaska Native Foods'. These 23 now sit BELOW the 60-band, as a floor rather than an override.
rules.unmappedPolicy: A category absent from all three maps does not fire. The row falls through to the name phrases and then to `other`. Report every unmapped value with its row count; do not invent entries.

rules.note: Classical therapeutic dravyas. Deliberately NOT filed under `supplement` — a vaidya would reject that framing — but capped and non-anchoring so they cannot constitute a meal.
Named pulses are listed individually rather than as a bare 'bean', because a bare 'bean' would beat G-SIDE on 'Beans, snap, green, raw' and turn a green vegetable into a main course.

Deliberately carries NO raw/dry veto. Rice is a staple whether or not it is cooked; edibility is the requiresCooking flag's job. rev1-draft had a veto here and it silently demoted 'Potatoes, flesh and skin, raw' and every raw grain row to `other`, which would have re-created the FC-1 `flesh` defect in a new place.
Bare 'seeds' was removed: it matched every 'X, mature seeds, raw' pulse row and routed dry legumes to side. The mature/dry seed veto is belt-and-braces on top of that removal.

rev2 CORRECTION. rev1 named `dravya.classification` and supplied a Sanskrit varga vocabulary with ZERO overlap with the data. The real field is `dravya.category` and its 19 values are English. All 19 are mapped. Counts: vegetable 107, spice 84, fruit 70, preparation 59, legume 44, beverage 44, medicinal 43, grain 36, regional 32, animal 30, leafy-green 29, dry-fruit-nut 26, dairy 22, oil-fat 20, fermented 18, seed 17, sweetener 14, herb 10, salt-mineral 9 = 714.

weakEntries.regional: 32 genuinely heterogeneous rows — morel mushroom, desert caper, palm vinegar, ghost chili, betel nut. Mapped to `other` rather than guessed.
weakEntries.fermented: 18 rows spanning kefir, tempeh, pickles, idli batter and fermented greens. Mapped to `condiment` because the smaller portion range is the safer error; name rules catch kefir, kombucha and tempeh above this.
weakEntries.preparation: 59 composed dishes — kitchari, upma, idli, dosa — but also ghee, lassi, golden milk and halwa. Those four are caught by name rules at 60, above this.

requiresCooking.purpose: Backs property C5. A row carrying this flag is ineligible as a plan component in any role.
requiresCooking.vetoIsTokenMatched: Each veto entry is a single token compared with the same plural tolerance as everything else. Do not write multi-word entries here; they will never fire.
requiresCooking.note: 'Peas, green, raw' and 'Beans, snap, raw' are ordinary raw vegetables and MUST NOT be flagged — that is what the green/fresh/snap vetoes are for. Nut headwords are deliberately absent from the list: raw almonds are food. Some raw legumes are not merely unpalatable but contain lectins that are actively toxic uncooked, which is why C5 is hard rather than soft.

isNearDuplicateOf.headwordExtraction: Normalize. If the first comma-delimited segment is a single token present in categoryPrefixTokens, drop it. From what remains, strip modifiers using modifiers.json. The headword is the first surviving content token, singularized. If nothing survives, fall back to the dropped prefix token.
isNearDuplicateOf.test: Two components are near-duplicates if their headwords are equal after singularization AND their roles are equal.

worked.comment: Correctly a duplicate: two rices in one meal is a variety defect, not a menu.

unknownPolicy.rule: `other` is eligible as a component but is never an anchor and is capped at 2 per meal, so an unresolved row can never by itself constitute a meal.
unknownPolicy.coverageGate: Over a 500-row stratified sample (proportional across the classical 336 / derived 1,969 / estimated 10,296 tiers) plus ALL 91 distinct food IDs the MP-6b sample selected, rows resolving to `other` must be at most 10%. Above that the taxonomy is not fit to constrain the solver and MP-7 must stop and report rather than tighten the solver against a map full of holes.

validation.crossDerivation: G12-style, and non-optional. Derive each row's role twice — once from name rules alone with the category map disabled, once from the category map alone with the name rules disabled — and enumerate every disagreement. Review them; do NOT auto-resolve. This is the only technique that found the `flesh` phrase matching 'Potatoes, flesh and skin, raw' across 46 vegetarian recipes, and a single-source check would not have found it.
validation.invalidComparators: Do not substitute a proxy signal for a missing one. G12 rev1 used 'not Vegan' as a stand-in for honey and produced 831 false disagreements out of 1,217. If a comparator does not exist, say so and stop.
validation.mustFail: Re-run the 21 verbatim meals from REPORT-MP6b.md through the C1-C9 checker. At least 12 of the 21 MUST fail at least one hard plausibility property, and all three infant-formula meals MUST fail C1. A suite written from observed failures that does not detect those failures is not evidence of anything.
validation.regression: All 45 properties, all 123 existing tests, exclusion goldens 117, resolution holdout 44/48. No regressions.

openForVaidya: Whether ashwagandha, shatavari and triphala belong in a meal plan at all, or only in a separate therapeutic list.
Whether ghee should be a component with its own portion, or an attribute of the dish it is cooked in.
Whether buttermilk/chaas at the end of a meal is a beverage or a digestive, which changes the C6 cap.
Whether a spice cap of 2 per meal is compatible with authored recipes that legitimately name a masala plus salt plus a tempering spice.

recipePostPass.purpose: rev4. Authored recipes cannot be classified by commodity name phrases, because a dish TITLE is made of ingredient names. Measured on the 1,500 authored recipes with the rev3 rules: 108 resolved to `herb` and 90 to `spice` — 13.2% of the recipe library — including 'Masala Vegetable Khichdi' (13 ingredients, lunch) as a spice and 'Ghee Ven Pongal' (10 ingredients) as a fat. `spice` caps at 2 per meal and 0.3-15 g, so those 198 recipes would have been effectively unusable. A further 79 fell to `other`, including every Mung Kitchari. This is a category error in the rev1-3 design, not a tuning miss.
recipePostPass.appliesTo: rows that are authored recipes with >=2 ingredients and >=1 preparation step (all 1,500 qualify)
recipePostPass.supersedes: A-RECIPE-COMPOSED, which is withdrawn. A-RECIPE-MEAL is retained as step 1.

steps.rule: meal == drink -> beverage; meal == dessert -> sweet. Direct, unchanged from A-RECIPE-MEAL.

truncate the title at a trailing ' with ' clause, strip parentheticals, then match `forms` against the TRAILING tokens, longest match wins. English dish names are head-final — the last content word names the form — which is why 'Coriander Chutney' is a condiment while 'Masala Vegetable Khichdi' is not a spice. The ' with ' truncation exists because 'Bajra Roti with Gud-Ghee' is a bread, not a fat.

ambiguousForms.masala: a blend when the recipe has <= 6 ingredients, a dish otherwise. 'Fennel Coriander Cooling Masala' (5 ingredients) is a spice blend; 'Black Bean Sweet Potato Masala' (9) is a curry. `churna`, `powder` and `blend` are unconditional — those words are never a dish.

steps.rule: otherwise meal in {breakfast, lunch, dinner} -> main; meal == snack -> side.

recipePostPass.prohibitedNote: A composed, cooked dish is never a raw seasoning leaf, a medicinal powder, a non-food, an ingredient-only row, a supplement or an infant product. `spice` and `fat` remain reachable, but ONLY from step 2 (an authored masala or a cultured ghee is a real preparation) — never from an ingredient token in the title.
recipePostPass.commodityRulesDoNotApply: For these rows the 95/92/80/70/60/50-band rules are skipped entirely. They were built for USDA commodity names and misfire on dish titles. The exclusionary detectors are not needed here either: an authored recipe is by construction not infant formula.
